offline_arms_llm: NONE — the offline arms are deterministic scripts vs naive verifiers; the throughput ratio is arithmetic, not opinion

cost_model.write_op: setting one JSON field value (an entry/edge is built field by field; identical rule both arms)
cost_model.hash_op: one sha256Hex over the house sealed-field grammar

weightings.h1: 1 hash-op = 1 write-op — the attacker-favorable absurd extreme (hashing free as writing)
weightings.verdict_rule: the kill fires if EITHER weighting lands D < 0.20 — a survival must hold even when hashing is priced free

cost_model.op_counters: counted in code as the attack scripts run (measured, not asserted by fiat)
notes: B2's registered 16 field writes per fake edge = the parenthesized 15 (cell, ts, before, after, delta{5}, imbalance, provenance{4}, chain) + v — an edge is built field by field including v=1; resolved as the registered NUMBER.

B3's '2 own balance writes' = the mutated edge's (before, after) pair; before is re-set to the unchanged running balance. Either reading costs identically and B2 dominates B3 at both weightings either way — T_signed is unaffected.

B3 iterates the mutation point from the tail backward (the registration's j=20 names the shape; the operationalization gives the attacker its BEST strategy, and suffix repairs are cheapest at the tail).

honest_cell.grammar: house edge-ledger grammar: v=1, cell=arena.credits.honest-cell-r9, delta={kind,ref,direction,amount,signed}, imbalance=0, provenance={origin:'arena-settlement',player,kind,ref}, chain=prior edge_hash (genesis null), edge_hash=sha256Hex(canonicalJson(SEALED_FIELDS)) via the published primitives (edge-ledger.edgeHash)

arm_A_unsigned.ledger: the same 40 entries as a plain settlement-input list {kind, amount, ts, ref} — the pre-chain (v0.1-era) posture: no balances, no seals, no chain
arm_A_unsigned.naive_verifier: the house's own validateSettlementInput (settlement.ts) — exactly what settlement checked before the v0.2 chain walk: schema-level only (known kinds, positive finite amounts, finite ts, non-empty refs)

A1.detail: every batch validated — the schema-level verifier is blind to forgery by construction

A2.detail: mutated amounts re-validate — nothing but schema exists to catch them

arm_B_signed.ledger: the honest 40-edge stone-v1-style chain over the same cell (sealed, linked, stranger-recomputable)
arm_B_signed.naive_verifier: the documented stranger walk (arena-gan-live.test.ts pattern): recompute every edge_hash from the SEALED_FIELDS [v, cell, ts, before, after, delta, imbalance, provenance] via canonicalJson + sha256Hex, check chain-link continuity (genesis null), check balance continuity (after = before + delta.signed)

kill_rule_verbatim: the economy-of-honesty hypothesis dies if signed forgery costs <20% less attack throughput in the registered offline arms
kill_rule_operationalization: T_arm = forged entries per attempt that pass the arm's naive verifier, one attempt = a fixed attacker op-budget W = 10000 ops against one honest cell. D = (T_unsigned - T_signed) / T_unsigned, T_signed = the attacker's BEST strategy across the registered signed attacks. SURVIVE iff D >= 0.20 in BOTH registered hash weightings; KILL iff D < 0.20 in either.
kill_rule_application: D(h1)=0.7648; D(h100)=0.9656 — every registered weighting clears the 0.20 line; the pre-registered kill does not fire
verdict: SURVIVE — the economy-of-honesty hypothesis holds in the registered offline arms: signed forgery costs ≥20% less attack throughput at BOTH registered weightings; the pre-registered kill does not fire
